subtitle: "Deploying a 108-resource stack, running it end to end, and what it took"

{{< include _generated/version-box.md >}}

## Verdict

**For the control plane, it works well, after a handful of non-obvious workarounds.** The final
stack applies cleanly from an empty emulator in about a minute. `tofu plan` then reports no
changes, and `tofu destroy` removes everything except one RDS-managed secret. Six of the 15
services in the stack needed an emulator-specific setting before OpenTofu could manage them. Every
one of those settings is a single switch in the code, so the same code still targets real AWS.

**For the data plane, it works within narrow limits.** A surprising amount behaves like AWS:

- REST API Gateway with Lambda authorizers, IAM policy evaluation (including inside Lambda),
  Lambda permissions;
- S3 range reads, the RDS Data API, Cognito password login with groups;
- CloudFront routing, caching and WAF;
- SQS, SNS, EventBridge schedules, Step Functions and DynamoDB streams;
- ALB → Lambda.

But the emulator **cannot run real application code**: Lambda is an embedded RustPython or QuickJS
interpreter, and Aurora is SQLite. Several edge and identity features are accepted by the API and
then silently ignored. Those are the dangerous kind of gap, because `tofu apply` succeeds.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Use it for
- Validating OpenTofu modules: resource wiring, IAM, naming, drift, destroy. It is fast, free and
  offline.
- Integration-testing **pure-Python or JS** Lambda logic against S3, DynamoDB, SQS, the RDS Data
  API and API Gateway.
- Exercising REST API authorizer and IAM designs. Here, 60 of 60 role × endpoint cases matched AWS.

## Don't use it for
- Anything with native dependencies: GDAL, numpy, titiler, tipg, FastAPI on pydantic v2, database
  drivers. The same goes for container-image Lambdas, ECS and EC2 workloads, which are lifecycle
  models only.
- Database behaviour: no PostGIS, SQLite semantics, and the Data API sees a different database
  from the wire endpoint.
- Security assertions about **HTTP API JWT authorizers** (signatures aren't verified),
  CloudFront Functions or response-header policies, or browser CORS.
:::

## What it took: the workarounds, in the order I hit them

| # | Symptom | Cause | Fix | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every SDK call: `AccessDenied: Sign the request with the emulator credentials` | the session's own `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` env vars win over the emulator's credentials file | `unset AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID …` in `scripts/emulator.sh env` | (setup) |
| 2 | `aws_s3_bucket: Still creating... [10m elapsed]` | provider 6.x reads tags via **S3 Control**; the account-id host prefix gives `000000000000.127.0.0.1:9297` | `skip_credentials_validation` + `skip_requesting_account_id`; build `execution_arn` from `aws_caller_identity` | [tofu-s3control-host-prefix](differences.qmd#tofu-s3control-host-prefix) |
| 3 | `aws_security_group`: `RevokeSecurityGroupEgress … InvalidPermission.NotFound` | new SGs lack AWS's default egress rule, which the provider revokes | no SG on the emulator | [ec2-sg-default-egress](differences.qmd#ec2-sg-default-egress) |
| 4 | `MasterUsername must be 1 to 16 letters or numbers; got 'features_admin'` | stricter validation (matches the API reference text) | `featuresadmin` | [rds-master-username-rule](differences.qmd#rds-master-username-rule) |
| 5 | `aws_rds_cluster`: `DescribeGlobalClusters … unrecognized filter name: db-cluster-id` | the provider uses an undocumented filter that AWS accepts | tried CloudFormation (#6), then a `terraform_data` + boto3 script read back by `data "aws_rds_cluster"` | [rds-describeglobalclusters-filter](differences.qmd#rds-describeglobalclusters-filter) |
| 6 | CloudFormation stack `CREATE_COMPLETE`, but its DB instance fails with "cluster not found" | CloudFormation (and Cloud Control) don't actually create RDS clusters | abandoned that route | [cfn-rds-not-materialized](differences.qmd#cfn-rds-not-materialized) |
| 7 | All authenticated calls get 401; authorizer log: `JWKS fetch … HTTPError 400` | in-Lambda HTTP to the Cognito JWKS URL is routed to Cognito's signed API | fetch the JWKS at deploy time (`data "http"`) into `JWKS_JSON` | [lambda-guest-http](differences.qmd#lambda-guest-http) |
| 8 | Through CloudFront: 401 with a valid token | the edge never forwards `Authorization` | authorizer also reads `X-Auth-Token` | [cloudfront-authorization-dropped](differences.qmd#cloudfront-authorization-dropped) |
| 9 | `plan` after `apply` wants to replace all API Gateway deployments | empty-vs-null computed attributes change the `triggers` hash | hash configured inputs only, normalise `authorizer_id` | [apigw-computed-attr-drift](differences.qmd#apigw-computed-attr-drift) |
| 10 | `aws_s3_object` keeps updating | multipart ETag ≠ MD5, **as on AWS** | `source_hash` | [s3-multipart-etag](differences.qmd#s3-multipart-etag) |
| 11 | `tofu destroy` fails on the DB subnet group | my cluster script didn't wait for the cluster to be gone | wait in the script | (my bug) |

Before any of this, the bigger decision: real titiler and tipg can't run, so I wrote pure-Python
stand-ins ([details](auth-api.qmd#what-was-built)). The stand-ins had to avoid loops over pixels,
because RustPython is slow at them, and use `bytes.translate`, slicing and big-int bit tricks
instead. A 256×256 tile then renders in 0.2–1.3 s on the emulator.

## Service by service (the main stack)

| Service | Resources managed by tofu | Out of the box? | Data plane in the stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| IAM | roles, inline policies | yes | enforced inside Lambda (least-privilege policies matter) |
| CloudWatch Logs | log groups | yes | Lambda `print()` output is queryable; that made debugging possible |
| Lambda | 5 zip functions (python3.12) | yes | runs, **on RustPython** |
| API Gateway (REST) | 4 APIs, authorizers, methods, integrations, gateway responses, deployments, stages, permissions | needed the drift fix (#9) | authorizers, IAM policy, Lambda permissions all enforced |
| Cognito | pool, client, 3 groups, 4 users, memberships | yes | `InitiateAuth`, refresh, `cognito:groups`; ES256 tokens |
| S3 | bucket, public access block, SSE, TLS-only policy, 2 objects | needed #2 | range GETs from Lambda |
| EC2/VPC | VPC, 2 subnets (security group dropped, #3) | partly | – |
| RDS | subnet group (+ cluster/instance via script) | **no** (#5) | Data API works; no PostGIS |
| Secrets Manager / KMS | via RDS-managed master secret | yes | Data API authenticates with it |
| CloudFront | distribution, cache policy | yes | routing and caching; drops `Authorization` and response headers |
| http / random / archive providers | JWKS fetch, passwords, zips | yes | – |

## Beyond the stack

{{< include _generated/probe-counts.md >}}

See the [probe results](probes.qmd) and the full [list of differences](differences.qmd).

Some positive surprises, where the emulator's fidelity goes well beyond stubbing:

- **IAM in Lambda.** Explicit and implicit denies in a Lambda's role are enforced, with AWS-style
  `AccessDenied` messages.
- **CloudFront.** Caches by policy (`x-cache: Hit from cloudfront`) and enforces **WAFv2** rules.
- **ECS.** Models image-pull *reachability* from the task's subnet routes. A subnet without a NAT
  or IGW gets `CannotPullContainerError … dial tcp public.ecr.aws:443: i/o timeout`.
- **ACM.** Refuses certificates for reserved TLDs (`.example`) just as AWS does.
- **Event sources.** EventBridge `rate(1 minute)` rules, SQS and DynamoDB-stream mappings, and
  S3 notifications actually invoke Lambdas.
- **ALBs.** Each gets a local listener that invokes Lambda targets.

Some negative surprises, where the API accepts the configuration and nothing happens:

- CloudFront Functions and response-headers policies;
- Cognito pre-token-generation output;
- user pool domains (no `/oauth2/token`);
- Python layers;
- CloudFormation RDS resources;
- ACM DNS validation (certificates stay `PENDING_VALIDATION`).

On top of these, the HTTP API (v2) JWT authorizer **lets forged tokens through**.

## Keeping this current

aws-emulator is under very active development: a new release (1.0.336) appeared during this
experiment. Each finding in `findings.toml` lists the emulator source paths and issue files it
depends on. `mise run update-check` reports which findings a new release could affect;
[UPDATE.md](https://github.com/ashiklom/simon-code-research/blob/main/aws-emulator-tofu/UPDATE.md)
has the full procedure.
